key_insight: ARGUS is an evidence-constrained agentic framework that combines LLM planning with deterministic genomics tools to avoid hallucinated variant interpretations and support uncertainty-aware decisions.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows how to build trustworthy research agents by separating reasoning from verification, enabling scalable interpretation of noncoding variants with real biological evidence sources.
method: Planner selects the next evidence source based on uncertainty and current findings.
Verifier deterministically evaluates outputs from 458 DNABERT-based TF-binding models plus external resources.
Investigation paths branch dynamically across ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE cCRE queries until a supported verdict or abstention is reached.
evidence_signal: On rs6983267, ARGUS produced divergent TF-specific outcomes using real ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE cCRE data, including a rescued false negative for FOXA1 and abstentions when evidence was weak or indirect.
watch_item: Performance depends on coverage and quality of underlying databases, so the system may still abstain or miss biology when direct experimental evidence is sparse.
paper_title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants
